request: Is a QALY a QALY, whoever gets it? Part 1: A QALY is a QALY

commands.speak: Some say a QALY is just neutral arithmetic, the same for everyone; others say it hides a moral choice about who counts.
Take our 60-year-old: standard care gives four years at a quality of 0.5, which is two QALYs.
The new treatment gives five years at 0.7, three and a half QALYs, and the gain between them is 1.5.
The sum asks how much health is gained, never whose — a QALY to this patient weighs exactly what it would to anyone else.
That is the first case for equal weighting: impartiality, no one's health counts for more because of who they are.
The second is the budget: the extra 30,000 spent here, at a threshold of 20,000 per QALY, would buy 1.5 QALYs for someone else.
So any extra weight for one group is health taken from patients we never see.
Yet the sum did choose something: it gave every person's QALYs a weight of one.
That is a moral choice too, so 'just arithmetic' is wrong.
Equal weighting is a defensible choice, not the absence of one.
And equal per QALY is not equal per person — which is where the critics begin.
